justification: Test-only change: realigns the BuilderReferralCard suite with the multi-step qualifier the component already ships (timeline -> ownership -> contact) and adds regression guards for the false-success defect. No production code is touched, no DB or API path changes. Minor tier because the blast radius is the test suite itself - but the suite guards a lead-capture surface where a silently-failed submit loses a paying lead, so the assertions are written to fail loudly rather than merely exercise the component.
functions: N/A - test file only. Adds two local helpers, advanceToContact() and fillContactAndSubmit(), that drive the 3 qualifier steps so each test starts from the contact form; no production function added or changed.
values: N/A - no runtime values read. The suite asserts on the posted payload (email, address, eligible, lga_name, interest_type, qualification{timeline,ownership}, consent_wording) and on PostHog event properties.
queries: N/A - no database access; the lead POST to /api/canibuildit/lead is mocked via global fetch.

break_it.scenario: The component regresses to showing the success confirmation even when the lead POST fails (the original false-success defect), and the suite still passes.
break_it.what_happens: A failed submit would be shown to the user as 'got your request', silently losing the lead with no retry prompt - the exact bug these tests exist to catch.
break_it.how: Two separate tests cover both failure modes (non-ok response, and a rejected fetch). Each asserts BOTH that the error text renders AND that the confirmation is absent (queryByText(/got your request/) not in document), so a regression that renders both cannot pass.
break_it.repro: Make the component call setSubmitted(true) in the catch/non-ok branch; both 'shows an error and NOT a confirmation' tests fail.

break_it.scenario: The consent-gating assertion matches the wrong element, so it passes without the error ever rendering.
break_it.what_happens: The test would go green whether or not the consent error appears, silently losing the guard on submitting contact details without consent.
break_it.how: 'tick the box' appears twice in the component - the consent error and the standing helper text under the checkbox - so getByText threw on ambiguity. The assertion now matches 'pass your details to the builder', which occurs only in the error string.
break_it.repro: grep the component: 'tick the box' returns 2 hits, 'pass your details to the builder' returns 1 (the error). Revert the matcher and the test fails with 'found multiple elements'.

break_it.scenario: The qualifier answers are dropped from the payload but the submit test still passes on the remaining fields.
break_it.what_happens: Leads would arrive without timeline/ownership qualification, degrading them to plain email-me rows and breaking builder routing, with no test failure.
break_it.how: The payload test asserts qualification toMatchObject({timeline:'asap', ownership:'owner'}) and consent_wording matching the referral-fee disclosure, in addition to the base fields; the event test asserts timeline/ownership/verdict on referral_lead_submitted.
break_it.repro: Remove qualification from the POST body; 'posts the referral interest_type + qualification ...' fails.

post_merge.db_reset: Not required - no schema or data change.
post_merge.manual_verify: Done: npx jest __tests__/components/tools/BuilderReferralCard.test.tsx -> 8/8 passed, including the previously-failing consent-gating test. Full frontend suite re-run clean: 68 suites / 904 tests passed.
